equity_bridge.item: Fair Work (award-covered salaried team member) provision, after tax
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR: provision 254 at 28 June 2026, expensed but not yet paid; 254 x (1 - 0.30). Orders and appeals outstanding, so the amount can still move.

equity_bridge.item: FY27 one-off program and restructuring costs, after tax
equity_bridge.note: Guided ~190 pre-tax in FY27 (Capability Centre dual-running, Liquor review and above-store redundancies) per the Analysis JSON guidance block; 190 x (1 - 0.30). Charged once in the bridge so the FY27 EBITDA margin path stays on the before-significant-items basis.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (7.0%) is more than double revenue (3.3%) and EPS (1.5%) CAGRs. Book equity is small (3.9bn against 45.7bn revenue) and grows through retention and the DRP, so it is not a usable growth anchor for a mature grocer; revenue CAGR is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series = operating cash flow - capex - lease principal - cash purchases of shares for employee plans. The 3-year FCF CAGR of 40% is a trough-to-recovery artefact: FY2023-FY2024 carried peak capex on the Witron automated distribution centres and Ocado customer fulfilment centres (capex 1,514 and 1,671). Statutory EPS is depressed in FY2026 by the 165 after-tax Fair Work provision; EPS before significant items was 93.8c (FY2025 82.6c).

scenario_narratives.base: Supermarkets keeps growing 3-4% (FY26: +3.7%, +5.1% ex tobacco, comparable sales +3.4%, eCommerce +26% to 13.6% of sales) while tobacco and Liquor (sales -3.3%, EBIT halved to 59) stay a drag, so group revenue grows ~3.5% fading to 2.5%. The FY26 step-up in margin (segment EBIT +9.9% on sales +2.8%) is kept and extended only slightly, to 9.5% EBITDA, as dual-running costs on the automated distribution and fulfilment centres are gone and Simplify and Save to Invest offsets wage inflation; the rest is reinvested in price under political and ACCC scrutiny. Net capex eases from 2.9% to 2.5% of revenue as the automation build finishes. Owner-FCF margin rises from ~2.2% to ~2.8%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The supply-chain automation and Ocado fulfilment centres deliver their full operating leverage, own-brand and retail media lift mix, eCommerce becomes margin-neutral or better, and Coles keeps taking share from Woolworths as it did through FY25-FY26. Revenue grows 4-4.5% early, EBITDA margin reaches 10%, and capex normalises quickly to 2.4% of revenue. This requires regulators to tolerate rising grocery margins, which is the main reason it carries less weight than base.
scenario_narratives.bear: The regulatory and competitive axes both go wrong: the December 2026 ACCC relief hearing on Down Down pricing extends the 12-product judgment across the 245 products with material penalties and class-action compensation, promotional mechanics are constrained, and a politically driven price reset plus Aldi, Costco and Amazon expansion and a recovered Woolworths force price reinvestment. Revenue grows ~2% (below food inflation plus population), EBITDA margin gives back the FY25-FY26 gains to 8.6%, Liquor does not recover, rents re-set upward and capex stays elevated for the new Victorian ADC and store renewals. Terminal multiple capped at 16x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Coles is a mature, defensive grocery duopolist valued on the cash left for owners after rent, on-market share purchases for staff plans, tax and net capex. Store leases are treated as a perpetual operating cost rather than debt. On that basis FY26 owner FCF is about A$0.9bn (~65c per share) against underlying NPAT of A$1.26bn; the gap is capex running ~1.4x non-lease depreciation. SBC is ~0.1% of revenue, so house and street values nearly coincide and the band carries no information.
key_risks_to_valuation: ACCC Down Down proceedings: liability found on 12 sample products (May 2026); relief hearing provisionally December 2026; penalties, extension to the other products and the follow-on class action are unprovisioned and NOT in the equity bridge
Fair Work underpayment matter: 254 provided (deducted after tax in the bridge); orders and appeals could increase it
Lease treatment: the perpetual lease charge is the largest single deduction (~3% of revenue against a ~2.2% owner-FCF margin); a 0.1pp change in lease cost or EBITDA margin moves value about 4-5%
Capex normalisation: base assumes net capex falls from 3.0% (FY27 guidance) to 2.5% of revenue after the Victorian ADC completes by FY30; if it stays near 3% value falls materially
Terminal value is roughly two-thirds of enterprise value and the 20x cap binds in base and bull
Liquor decline and tobacco sales erosion dilute group growth below the Supermarkets headline

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 20.10-24.75
data_sources.financials: COL.AX_Metrics.csv and kpis table (FY2019-FY2026); FY2026 annual report (52 weeks ended 28 June 2026) for the cash flow statement, segment note, lease note, contributed equity and the Fair Work/ACCC disclosures
data_sources.qualitative: COL.AX_Analysis.json (growth drivers, risks, FY27 guidance, bull/bear cases) and the FY2026 annual report (financial review, legal proceedings).

inputs.share_count_basis: 1,343.1m ordinary shares on issue at 28 June 2026 (FY26 AR contributed-equity note), which includes shares held in trust for employee plans; weighted diluted count is 1,342m. Held FLAT: awards are satisfied by on-market purchases already charged in the flows, and the ~1.8m/yr DRP issue is scrip in lieu of cash dividend at market, value-neutral.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: Operating cash flow 3,344 (already after 426 lease interest) less purchase of PP&E and intangibles 1,491 less principal elements of lease payments 940. The Metrics CSV FreeCashFlow of 1,853 is OCF less capex before lease principal and is not an owner figure for a lessee of ~850 supermarkets.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report: share-based payments expense 24 (cash-flow reconciliation); cash 'Purchase of shares to satisfy the employee equity incentive and share plans' 45 (financing). The cash purchase is the real cost of keeping the count flat and has exceeded the expense in every year since FY2023, so 45 is the figure charged. Interest received is 3 against net DEBT, so nothing is stripped.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: last Sunday of June (FY2026: 52 weeks ended 28 June 2026)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD build: ~4.4% Australian 10-year government bond, ~5.5% equity risk premium, beta ~0.6 for a defensive grocery duopolist gives a cost of equity near 7.7%; after-tax cost of BBB+/Baa1 debt ~4%. With leases treated as an operating cost the financial debt weight is only ~4% of enterprise value, so WACC is ~7.5%. The same 7.5% is used in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the flows and the weights, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full cash lease payment (FY26: 940 principal in financing + 426 interest in operating = 1,366, 2.99% of revenue) is charged inside EBIT every year via lease_cost_pct_path, and in the terminal value in perpetuity. The 8,092 of AASB 16 lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt; adding them as well would charge the same store rent twice. D&A in the model is ex right-of-use depreciation (1,898 total less 959 ROU = 939). Capitalised at the model's own rate the perpetual lease charge is worth roughly 3x the balance-sheet liability, so this is the harsher of the two valid treatments for a retailer that must renew its leases forever.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company; dcf-methods routing row 'non-US operating company' with the lease, SBC-near-zero and AUD-WACC adaptations). FRESH BUILD, no prior valuation. EBITDA is the company's segment EBITDA before significant items (FY26 4,220; statutory 3,985 after the 235 Fair Work provision). Margins are on total revenue 45,722 (sales revenue 45,580 plus other operating revenue). Capex is modelled NET of property sale proceeds (FY26 1,491 gross less 163 proceeds = 1,328), because Coles develops and then sells-and-leases-back store property and the resulting rent is in the lease line. FY0 tie: modelled EBIT 1,915 x 0.70 less after-tax interest on borrowings ~70 = ~1,270 against reported NPAT before significant items of 1,255. Working capital: payables (4,711) exceed inventory plus receivables (3,281), so growth releases cash; capture set at 2% of the revenue increase, below the ~3% the balance sheet implies. Flat share count is funded: Coles buys shares on market for its plans (45 in FY26). Data flag: the CSV StockBasedComp column is one year late for FY2024-FY2026 (shows 37/28/27; filings say 28/27/24). The annual report carries no quantified FY27 guidance; the FY27 capex (~1.55bn) and one-off cost (~190) figures are taken from the Analysis JSON guidance block (FY26 results presentation and Q1 FY27 update), neither of which is in Extracted/, so they are unverified against a primary document here.

base.rationale: FY26 actuals: EBITDA before significant items 9.23% of revenue (FY25 8.86%), lease cash 2.99%, D&A ex-ROU 2.05%, net capex 2.90%, tax 30% statutory (effective 29.6%). D&A rises as the ADC/CFC asset base (PP&E +9.4% in FY26) depreciates; net capex eases toward 2.5% as the automation program completes, leaving capex ~1.09x D&A at maturity, consistent with ~2.5% nominal growth. FY27 capex guidance of ~1.55bn gross (Analysis JSON, FY26 results and Q1 FY27 update) less ~150 of property proceeds is ~3.0% of revenue net; capex stays near 2.9-3.0% until the Victorian ADC (Truganina, ~880m, commissioning by FY30) is complete, then eases.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): there is no balance-sheet risk (BBB+/Baa1, 2.3x lease-adjusted leverage) but a live single-regulator exposure, with ACCC penalties unquantified and unprovisioned and the relief hearing weeks away. Base 55%: grocery demand is stable and the FY26 margin level is already in the run-rate. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs continued share gains, full automation payback and regulatory tolerance of a 10% EBITDA margin at the same time.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
